title: What We Are - Quantum Theatre
text:
What We Are - Quantum Theatre
# What We Are ## Mission Statement Quantum Theatre is a company of progressive, professional artists dedicated to producing intimate and sophisticated theatrical experiences in uncommon settings, exploring universal themes of truth, beauty, and human relationships in unexpected ways. ### Quantum Theatre is a kind of laboratory… an incubator for the amazing, christened in 1990, rededicated each year with the rites of spring to its mission to bring forth artists forging new theatrical ground. They are playwrights, directors, actors, influencers. They come from Pittsburgh, from around the country, and from around the world. Productions are staged environmentally in places that aren’t theatres. Quantum’s artists mine all kinds of non-traditional spaces for the sensory possibilities they offer when combined with creative design. We find it meaningful to place the audience and performers together, the moving parts inside the works. “Sometimes there’s singing. Often a sunset. Always a reaction.” ### Our Work The shows run the gamut from those you thought you knew but now experience like never before, to shows that didn’t exist until their elements mixed in our laboratory. We want to move people with our experiments. We believe that the theatre has limitless ability to put people in motion.

title: What We Are - Quantum Theatre
text:
What We Are - Quantum Theatre
We want to move people with our experiments. We believe that the theatre has limitless ability to put people in motion. If any art can transform, open a mind, the theatre can. We are interested in real life and how it intersects with a theatrical experience—resulting in plays staged outside where a moon may rise, or not, or an urban excavation where street noises will infiltrate, or a warehouse in winter where the audience might need blankets… then watch a performer strip naked and take a shower. We’re looking for truthfulness, knowing that the word is a slippery slope. We give voice to artists who invest deeply and touch the personal, even as they tell a tale, a far-off, magical, scary, too-close-to-home, knee-slapping, sob-inducing tale. #### Supporters Our supporters help us produce our unique, intimate, and sophisticated theatrical experiences all over the region. Let Quantum Theatre move you in new, unexpected ways. ## _radio island_ A World Premiere. Written by Liza Birkenmeier Directed by Katie Brook _radio island_ tells the story of an international hostage negotiator who returns to her childhood home where global and local worlds collide as memory, family, and buried histories surface. What begins as a homecoming in this gothic thriller becomes something far less predictable – a reckoning with people, places, and unfinished business that whispers ‘silence is more dangerous than you think.’ Starring Siovhan Christensen and Helena Ruoti Featuring Treasure Treasure #### SHOWTIMES October 23 – November 15, 2026 Tuesday – Sunday at 8pm Sunday Matinee: October 25 at 2pm Staged inside at Rockwell Park ## _Cassandra_ A World Premiere. In this original and immersive experience, you’ll discover a web of intimacy and control where nothing is quite what it seems. The question lingers: what does it cost to believe? #### SHOWTIMES April 9 – May 2, 2027 Wednesday – Saturday at 8pm Saturday and Sunday at 2pm

Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre
# Meet the Team ### Quantum Theatre’s work thrives thanks to the collaboration of a strong administrative team and experienced production crew who specialize in site-specific work to support ambitious programming. ##### Executive Director ### Julie DeSeyn Julie is an accomplished nonprofit executive with more than two decades of leadership experience across the arts, human services, philanthropy, and community development. She brings deep expertise in building sustainable business models, fostering collaborative and high-performing teams, and advancing ambitious goals with limited resources. Known for her creative and innovative approach to problem-solving, Julie excels at cultivating community partnerships, strengthening trust, and leading effective fundraising efforts. She has served as Executive Director of Quantum since February 2023. ##### Associate Director ### Nate Madden Nate graduated from the University of Pittsburgh in 2023 with a BA in Religious Studies. He manages Quantum Theatre’s data and development processes and oversees patron experience operations. ##### Associate Director ### Kelley Bowen Kelley studied theatre at The College of William & Mary and Boston University. She began her professional career as an actress in Pittsburgh, and as an assistant director with the Three Rivers Shakespeare Festival and Boston’s Huntington Theatre Company.

title: Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre

Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre
Kelley studied theatre at The College of William & Mary and Boston University. She began her professional career as an actress in Pittsburgh, and as an assistant director with the Three Rivers Shakespeare Festival and Boston’s Huntington Theatre Company. After film, tv, and commercial work in Los Angeles, she held development and literary roles at South Coast Repertory and Merrimack Repertory Theatre, and now supports communication, events, and community partnerships at Quantum. ##### Associate Producer and Patron Relations Manager ### Hazy J Hazy is a Youngstown State University alumnus with their BFA in Theatre Studies and a minor in Music. Hazy has worked professionally as a house manager and stage manager in Pittsburgh and Youngstown for more than five years and is proud to work with the administrative and production teams to continuously improve the patron experience. ##### Director of Production ### Alex Ungerman Alex Ungerman has directed 48 plays and produced 60. His work has appeared at Fringe Festivals around the country, and twice at the Edinburgh Fringe. He co-founded _The Grassroots Shakespeare Company_ in 2009–which has produced Shakespeare around the world, including: Utah, Arizona, Washington D.C., and London.

Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix 2026 | PVGP | Visit Pittsburgh
# Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Motorsport Festival Experience a world-class, one-of-a-kind automotive event inside a city park! The **Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix** (PVGP), celebrating its 44th anniversary in 2026, is the nation's largest vintage street race and the only one staged on public roads. Dates, Location & Parking Admission Vintage Grand Prix Festival Map Schedule FAQs ## Dates, Location & Parking ### Dates July 11 - 19, 2026 ### Location Schenley Park ### Parking Public parking on race weekend at Schenley Park is available on Flagstaff Hill, across the street from Phipps Conservatory. There are also free air-conditioned shuttle buses to the golf course and over to the Start/Finish line. You can pre-purchase your parking pass and save $5, and have a guaranteed spot. ## Admission A $20 weekend admission donation (ages 13+) helps cover event costs and supports our charity partners. Children 12 and under are free. title: The Museum - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:
The Museum - The Andy Warhol Museum
We are one of the most comprehensive single-artist museums in the world and the largest in North America. The Warhol is one of the four Carnegie Museums, and a collaborative project between Carnegie Institute, Dia Art Foundation, and The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Inc. Plans to house The Warhol in Pittsburgh were announced in 1989, and the museum opened its doors during a 24-hour celebration on May 13, 1994. Originally built in 1911 as a distribution center for products sold to mills and mines, The Warhol was redesigned by architect Richard Gluckman and features seven floors of gallery and exhibition space as well as an underground level that houses The Factory education studio and the conservation lab. Established in 1895 by Andrew Carnegie, Carnegie Museums is a collection of four distinct museums: Carnegie Museum of Art, Carnegie Museum of Natural History, Kamin Science Center, and The Andy Warhol Museum. The museums reach more than 1.4 million people a year through exhibitions, educational programs, outreach activities, and special events.

title: The Collection - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:

The museum also houses the entire Andy Warhol Video Collection – over 2,300 videotapes which include all episodes and outtakes of his television series _Fashion_ , _Andy Warhol’s T.V._ , and _Andy Warhol’s_ _Fifteen Minutes_ , the soap operas _Vivian’s Girls_ , _Phoney_ , and _Fight_ , and the large body of work known as _Factory Diaries_. The film and video collection is critical to understanding the artist Andy Warhol. From the time he obtained his first film camera in 1963 until his death in 1987, Warhol actively explored the moving image, creating epic films, personal portraits, cable television shows, and music videos. His films and video capture the rich and raw texture of the fertile cultural milieu in which he lived and worked. title: The Collection - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:
The Collection - The Andy Warhol Museum
## The museum The museum’s collection includes works from the artist’s entire artistic output—from 1940s student work to 1980s collaborations. Our seven-story museum devotes four floors to showcasing an ever-changing selection of Warhol’s artwork, as well as features a permanent film and video gallery for viewing individual Warhol films and videos. One floor is devoted to the museum’s archives collection, and another is reserved for rotating exhibitions of deep dives into the museum’s collection or showcasing contemporary artists that resonate with Warhol. The ground floor continuously shows Fifteen Minutes Eternal, a twenty-minute introductory film, and the underground includes The Factory education studio and the museum’s conservation lab. ## Exhibition Rentals Our curatorial team develops traveling exhibitions that are available to rent for display at museums around the world. title: Sharif Bey: Homecoming - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:
Sharif Bey: Homecoming - The Andy Warhol Museum
Drawing from the artist’s experiences across various creative communities, residencies and partnerships, this exhibition celebrates Bey’s return to his hometown and the wealth of techniques, connections and artistic insights he brings back with him. Bey creates complex sculptures inspired by modernism, functional pottery and Oceanic and African art. With references to childhood memories of Pittsburgh’s urban landscape, his work provides commentary on identity and home that has multiple interpretations: the physical return to a meaningful place of origin, an introspective journey through personal history and memory, and a reconnection with artistic roots and traditions. Bey’s monumental ceramic sculptures will be exhibited alongside artwork from our permanent collection by Andy Warhol and Jean-Michel Basquiat. All three artists engage deeply with themes of identity, culture and societal commentary, and their shared and diverging histories create dynamic dialogues on the complexity of American art. _Homecoming_ celebrates community arts education and highlights Pittsburgh’s enduring role as a crucible for artistic innovation, continuing the city’s rich tradition of supporting local communities and artists—an essential factor in Sharif Bey’s development and emergence as a significant voice in contemporary art.

title: Sharif Bey: Homecoming - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:
Sharif Bey: Homecoming - The Andy Warhol Museum
This volume commemorates Pittsburgh-born ceramic artist, sculptor and educator Sharif Bey’s (born 1974) return to his hometown for a momentous exhibition at The Andy Warhol Museum. Bey creates complex sculptures inspired by modernism, functional pottery and Oceanic and African art. Incorporating references to childhood memories of Pittsburgh’s urban landscape, his work offers layered commentary on identity and home, probing the multiple interpretations of each concept. In the book, reproductions of Bey’s monumental ceramics are placed in dialogue with artworks by Andy Warhol and Jean-Michel Basquiat, pulled from the museum’s permanent collection. Altogether, Homecoming celebrates community arts education and highlights, through multiple texts, Pittsburgh’s enduring role as a crucible for artistic development—a key factor in Bey’s emergence as a mighty voice in contemporary art. title: About — Photo Antiquities Museum of Photographic History
text:
About — Photo Antiquities Museum of Photographic History
**About Us** # Step back in time and experience the history of the world through the lens of a camera. Photo Antiquities Museum of Photographic History was founded in 1993 to preserve and present the history of photography. Through the use of original photographic images and the equipment used to capture them, the museum strives to achieve its mission. Guided tours, educational programming and collaboration with non-profit organizations and museum members contribute to the continued growth and development of the museum. With the introduction of the Daguerreotype in 1839, it immediately became apparent that this process of photographic imaging was worthy of preserving. As the science of photography progressed, Ambrotypes, Tintypes and early paper processes all aided in recording history. As our ability evolved to capture images through the use of film, motion pictures, Polaroid, video and digital media, the requirement to preserve these images and equipment has become greater. With technological advances, many stored digital images are no longer printed and can be deleted electronically forever. Preservation of historic images and equipment becomes more important as we move to the next chapter in the evolution of photography. ## **HOURS** ### **Photo Antiquities is currently offering tours by appointment only**

Skip To Main Content Pause All Rotators # About Us -- Point Park University Athletics Point Park University is a provisional member of the National Collegiate Athletics Association (NCAA) and the Mountain East Conference (MEC). PPU competes in NCAA Division II. The Pioneers sponsor 20 varsity sports that compete at the intercollegiate level. Athletics scholarships are awarded to student-athletes as allowed by the NCAA. Since joining NCAA Division II, Point Park had added five sports, including four that began competing in 2025-26 (men's and women's lacrosse, men's and women's wrestling). Women's flag football will begin competing in 2026-27. Point Park University announced that it was accepted by the NCAA for provisional membership in Division II beginning on July 11, 2024. The Pioneers were previously a member of the NAIA for more than 50 years. The school was founded in 1933, and the Pioneers became members of the NAIA in 1967. As a NAIA school, Point Park won numerous conference championships and has been represented at many NAIA National Championship events (across multiple sports). Point Park is a member of the Mountain East Conference, which is comprised of 11 members institutions across four different states: West Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Ohio.

title: Conservation – The Westmoreland Museum of American Art
text:
Conservation – The Westmoreland Museum of American Art
**Conservation** The Westmoreland Museum of American Art houses a diverse permanent collection of over 4,000 objects, including paintings, works on paper, sculptures, and decorative arts. Many of these pieces are considered treasures of American art, making their proper care and conservation critical to preserving their value and integrity for future generations. ##### **Collection Care** The Museum employs stringent environmental controls to protect its collection from deterioration. These include the following: * Temperature and Humidity Control: The Museum maintains a stable environment with carefully regulated temperature and humidity levels to prevent damage. * Light Regulation: Light exposure is a significant factor in the degradation of artwork. The Museum uses controlled light levels, and frames are equipped with UV-protective glass that blocks 99% of harmful ultraviolet light. To further protect sensitive pieces, their time on display is limited. ##### **Works on Paper** For works on paper, the Museum uses high-quality archival materials. These include acid-free, neutral, or basic pH paper for matting and mounting. The Museum also ensures that UV-protective glass shields these works, blocking harmful rays that can cause fading and discoloration. ##### **Sculptures** Sculptures are displayed on stable surfaces to prevent movement and potential damage.

title: Conservation – The Westmoreland Museum of American Art
text:
Conservation – The Westmoreland Museum of American Art
##### **Sculptures** Sculptures are displayed on stable surfaces to prevent movement and potential damage. They are regularly dusted with soft, chemical-free cloths or gentle brushes made of goat hair to keep them clean without causing wear or scratches. #### **Handling and Conservation** Museum staff are trained to handle objects with the utmost care, using clean, dry hands or gloves to avoid transferring oils, dirt, or moisture to the surfaces. When damage does occur, professional conservators—experts skilled in chemistry, art, and art history—are engaged to restore the piece. #### **Conservation Treatments** Conservation treatments are approached with a focus on reversibility and respect for the artist’s original intent. Prior to any work, conservators document the piece with photographs and written reports. These same steps are taken following the treatment to ensure a complete record of the restoration process. By employing these meticulous preservation methods, The Westmoreland ensures that its treasured collection will continue to be enjoyed for years to come. If you have any questions about our collection or the conservation process, please don’t hesitate to reach out. For more details, please contact Doug Evans, Director of Collections & Exhibition Management: dwevans@thewestmoreland.org. ## **Conservation Corner**

title: About Us | Bach Choir of Pittsburgh
text:
About Us | Bach Choir of Pittsburgh
# About Us ## _Choral performance like you’ve not seen before._ ## What We Do Bach Choir of Pittsburgh (BCP) was founded in 1934 to perform works of Johann Sebastian Bach exclusively. Under the leadership of Conductor and Artistic Director Thomas W. Douglas, the choir continues to evolve from a narrowly-focused ensemble to a larger, more inclusive choir that performs major choral works by composers from the Renaissance through the present. After its inception the Bach Choir grew from 60 to 100 singers, and it currently remains steady with 75 members, including a 16-person core of paid professional singers. BCP produces a three-production concert season that is presented in unique venues in and around Pittsburgh, in addition to a Summer Sing educational program in June of each year. Auditions for choir and professional core positions are held on an annual basis. In addition to our regular concert season, the Bach Choir is available for hire throughout the tri-state area. The Choir is critically acclaimed for its innovative, precise, and entertaining concert performances.

# Audition and Membership ## _Join the BCP Family – Sing with the Bach Choir!_ Auditions for the 26-27 season will be held on the evening of August 25, 2026. If you would like to audition, please fill out the form below. The Auditions Coordinator will contact you to make arrangements for you to audition. Questions regarding auditions should be sent to auditions@bachchoirpittsburgh.org The Bach Choir of Pittsburgh includes a core of professional, paid singers and also volunteer singers. The audition process for both categories are listed below. We welcome everyone to audition and are looking to diversify and expand our choir. ## AUDITION PROCESS **Regular Member Auditions (5 Minutes in Length):** * Sing one prepared piece (bring a copy of music for the accompanist) * Sight sing **Core Auditions (10 Minutes in Length):** * Sing two memorized songs in two different languages. (bring music for the accompanist) * Sight sing. * Oral testing (keys, chords, musical terms, etc.) and aural tests (scales, intervals, etc.) will also be part of your audition session For singers whose are chosen to join the choir, an orientation session for new members will be held when rehearsals start in September.

All choir members must re-audition for each season. ## MEMBERSHIP INFORMATION To join the Choir is an opportunity to participate in making great music together with the conductor and your fellow singers, and a expectation to attend the rehearsals and the concerts for the entire season. The Choir’s rehearsal and subscription season runs from late August through early May. Rehearsals are held each Tuesday evening from 7:30 pm to 10:00 pm at Rodef Shalom Congregation, 4905 Fifth Avenue in Oakland. Rehearsals usually begin the first Tuesday after Labor Day and end in early May following the last scheduled season concert. There are two dress rehearsals, typically the Thursday and Friday evening before each concert weekend, which all members are required to attend. Concerts are typically Saturday evening and Sunday afternoon. A half-day, Saturday choir retreat may also be required during the fall or spring, depending on the difficulty of the music and concert schedule.

title: Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
text:
Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
BRADENTON, Fla. -- Dozens of prospects have filled the halls, classrooms and workout facilities at Pirate City over the past few weeks for the Forge High Performance Camp. None of them are built like Tony Blanco Jr. Then again, Blanco this week said he’s 6-foot-7, 290 pounds. There aren't many baseball players in Bradenton or anywhere else on the planet who look like offensive tackles. And, of course, possess the power to go along with that imposing build. "His ability to impact the ball is at the top of Minor League Baseball in terms of the raw power, exit velocities that he gets, hard-hit rate, etc." said Pirates director of coaching and player development Michael Chernow. "When he touches it, it goes a long way. It goes really far." Blanco has literally and figuratively been a gigantic project for the Pirates. But the 21-year-old first baseman also enjoyed his best season yet in 2026, more than doubling what he’s done since his Dominican Summer League debut in 2022. The games played, the production, the learning, the staying healthy. That's what matters most with Blanco.

title: Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
text:
Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
The games played, the production, the learning, the staying healthy. That's what matters most with Blanco. In 84 contests -- all but four at High-A Greensboro -- Blanco hit .253 with an .896 OPS. He finished with 25 home runs, 17 doubles, and 60 RBIs, slugging .558. Among Pirates prospects, only Murf Gray, Jhonny Severino, Edward Florentino and Lonnie White Jr. homered more. But those guys averaged 114 games -- 30 more than Blanco. Which frames part of the narrative here: Can Blanco stay healthy long enough to gain traction? Prior to this year, Blanco’s high-water mark for games played in a season was 40 in Rookie ball in 2024. He missed the first three months in 2025 and about a month last year due to hamstring injuries. It’s why Chernow said the No. 1 focus with Blanco involves staying on the field. “The thing that’s super intriguing about him -- this plays into staying on the field; obviously we want guys staying on the field -- is that the more plate appearances he’s gotten over time, he’s showing us signs that he possesses the ability to be a well-rounded hitter,” Chernow said. Blanco’s physical tools certainly impressive.

title: Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
text:
Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
“The thing that’s super intriguing about him -- this plays into staying on the field; obviously we want guys staying on the field -- is that the more plate appearances he’s gotten over time, he’s showing us signs that he possesses the ability to be a well-rounded hitter,” Chernow said. Blanco’s physical tools certainly impressive. A year ago in the Arizona Fall League, Blanco had a 464-foot homer and a 120.4 mph double on back-to-back days. Blanco won the Home Run Derby, blasting one 122.9 mph in the process. To Chernow’s point, the list of people who can hit a baseball as hard and far as Blanco is very short -- Oneil Cruz, Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton and maybe a few others. “I thank God for allowing me to have that power,” Blanco said, with mental performance coach Jose Corrales translating. “It feels good to hit the ball hard and far.” Blanco also knows success involves more than power, hence why he’s been pouring his efforts into the Forge camp. He's working on his body to improve athleticism, sure, but also to perfect routines to prepare every day and maintain health over a full season.

title: Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly

Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
Blanco also knows success involves more than power, hence why he’s been pouring his efforts into the Forge camp. He's working on his body to improve athleticism, sure, but also to perfect routines to prepare every day and maintain health over a full season. Along with injuries, another point of emphasis with Blanco has been strikeouts. Given his profile, they’re going to happen. But Blanco feels there was important progress made on that front in 2026, the right-handed hitter cutting his strikeout rate from 35.1% over his previous pro seasons to 29.5% this past summer. Beyond the numbers, Blanco felt he learned more about patience and how he was being pitched, how pitchers nibbled and tried hard to get him to chase. That increased the importance of Blanco identifying a plan for success and sticking with it, something he believes he did far better after returning from the hamstring injury on July 24. “That aspect of game is hard because pitchers know me,” Blanco said. “They know I have power and want to take me away from my plan. “There was a period of time where I was being too aggressive and chasing too many pitches.

title: Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly
text:
Pirates set coaching staff for '26 under manager Kelly

# Penguins Announce 2026.27 Gate Giveaway Promotional Schedule By Pittsburgh Penguins August 25, 2026 * Link copied The Pittsburgh Penguins 2026.27 home schedule will feature 16 fan-favorite gate giveaways throughout the season, enhancing the PPG Paints Arena game experience. Highlights of the promotional schedule include two Evgeni Malkin-themed giveaway items, including an Evgeni Malkin Talking Bobblehead presented by The DICK’S Sporting Goods Foundation on January 23 versus Vancouver and an Evgeni Malkin Coffee Table Book presented by Highmark on February 28 against the Rangers. In addition, fans will be able to take home a Mike Lange Catchphrase Alarm Clock on December 5 versus New Jersey, celebrating the legacy of the former voice of the Penguins. The Penguins will celebrate the team’s 60th anniversary with special in-game moments throughout the year beginning with the home opener versus the Montreal Canadiens. Commemorative anniversary giveaways include a 60th anniversary poster on December 18, followed by a 60th anniversary patterned shirt giveaway on March 14, presented by Levin Furniture & Mattress.

Once you design it, we’ll fire it, so that all pieces become one. Participants will work seated in our climate-controlled Classroom and with room temperature pieces of glass. You will begin with a glass tile that acts as your “canvas,” then arrange the colorful glass granules and thin glass strands into a design of your choosing. Once the designs are complete, suncatchers are placed in a kiln overnight to melt (fuse) together forever. Suitable for ages 5 and up. |

# Point Park History A proud institution with a rich history and a bright future Images from the Archives — 11 images Business Technical College Medical Secretarial Division - 1955 Business Technical College - 1958 Point Park Junior College Sign Installation on Academic Hall - 1962 Academic Hall - 1963 Academic Hall with the Sherwyn Hotel (later to become Lawrence Hall) in the background - 1963 Black Diamond II, Point Park's live bison mascot, lived in South Park. – 1967 Black Diamond II mascot with Pioneer Girl - 1967 Construction of the skybridge between Academic and Lawrence Halls - 1968 The interior of Colonial Trust Bank, which later became the University Center library. Point Park U-Trolley – 1973 Students on the skybridge - 1976 Throughout its history, Point Park University has taken pride in its urban roots and contributions to the vitality of Downtown Pittsburgh. The University began as a small business training college in 1933 under the direction of Dorothy Finkelhor and L. Herbert Finkelhor. By 1960, the business school had grown to more than 800 students and moved into the building now known as Academic Hall, on Wood Street in Downtown Pittsburgh.

title: Point Park History | Point Park University | Pittsburgh, PA
text:
Point Park History | Point Park University | Pittsburgh, PA
Herbert Finkelhor. By 1960, the business school had grown to more than 800 students and moved into the building now known as Academic Hall, on Wood Street in Downtown Pittsburgh. That year it became known as Point Park Junior College, named for the city's historic Point State Park. The junior college soon added programs in engineering technology, education, and journalism, and acquired performing arts space at The Pittsburgh Playhouse in the Oakland neighborhood. In 1966 the college was granted four-year status, officially becoming Point Park College, and began awarding bachelor's degrees. Point Park's first graduate program (in journalism and mass communication) was established in 1981. Dance and theatre programs were introduced, which laid the groundwork for Point Park's current Conservatory of Performing Arts. After weathering a severe financial crisis in the mid-1990's, Point Park emerged to implement a new strategic plan and dramatically boost enrollment. In 2003, it achieved university status and became Point Park University. The University's comprehensive strategic planning process continued, focusing on enhancing academic excellence, a quality student experience, managed growth and community engagement.

title: Point Park History | Point Park University | Pittsburgh, PA
text:
Point Park History | Point Park University | Pittsburgh, PA
In 2003, it achieved university status and became Point Park University. The University's comprehensive strategic planning process continued, focusing on enhancing academic excellence, a quality student experience, managed growth and community engagement. In 2008, Point Park moved into the next chapter of its development as a vibrant academic and community partner with the announcement of the Academic Village at Point Park University, a thriving living and learning hub. Point Park's $244 million campus and public enhancement space plan, including the development of Village Park, was completed in 2011. Continuing its long tradition of excellence in journalism, the University opened the Center for Media Innovation in 2016. This state-of-the-art incubator and collaborative space features TV and radio/podcast studios, a photo studio and multimedia newsroom. In 2018, the Pittsburgh Playhouse was relocated to Forbes Avenue in Downtown Pittsburgh. The Playhouse provides world-class professional spaces for both unconventional and classical presentations developed by the faculty, students and visiting artists of the Conservatory of Performing Arts. President Chris W. Brussalis unveiled the newest strategic plan, Pioneer Vision 2030, in October 2023.

title: Point Park History | Point Park University | Pittsburgh, PA
text:
Point Park History | Point Park University | Pittsburgh, PA
President Chris W. Brussalis unveiled the newest strategic plan, Pioneer Vision 2030, in October 2023. The plan looks to leverage the University's strengths as a premier conservatory of performing arts and create synergistic programs with the five other schools within the University. On a grander scale, the plan includes a strategy for impacting Downtown Pittsburgh and igniting a third renaissance of the city. Today, the University enrolls approximately 3,300 full- and part-time students in more than 100 undergraduate, master's, doctoral and certificate programs offered through its Rowland School of Business, School of Arts and Sciences, School of Communication, School of Education, and the School of Dance and School of Theatre, Film and Animation in the Conservatory of Performing Arts. Its students represent 48 states/territories and 44 countries. Nearly a century later, that vision lives on in a thriving university rooted in Downtown Pittsburgh and a close-knit, career-ready community._ _ Point Park University is celebrating its first annual Founder’s Day by honoring exceptional supporters of the school and establishing a way for alumni to donate their graduation regalia to students who may not be able to afford the appropriate attire. Point Park’s roots go back to Feb. 6, 1933, when Dorothy C. Finkelhor established the Business Training College in Downtown Pittsburgh during the Great Depression, specifically to provide people with the professional training they would need to work in an office setting. “Dorothy Finkelhor established the Business Training College with a belief in the importance of practical, hands-on education at a time when jobs were scarce and people were desperate,” said Dr. Chris W.

“Dorothy Finkelhor established the Business Training College with a belief in the importance of practical, hands-on education at a time when jobs were scarce and people were desperate,” said Dr. Chris W. Brussalis, president of Point Park University. “Point Park has continued that legacy by focusing on experiential learning and a personalized support system to ensure our students have success as professionals.” The weekend celebration includes the establishment of the **President’s Distinguished Achievement Awards**. Separate from any other institutional recognition, these awards are bestowed solely at the discretion of the president. The inaugural class of six people will be honored for their significant contributions to the Point Park University community. #### Pittsburgh Playhouse Presents "The Chief" Professor Philip Winters stars in "The Chief," directed by alumnus Justin Fortunato. The weekend will include the Pittsburgh Playhouse production of “The Chief,” the one-man play that brings the spirit of Pittsburgh football and the legacy of Art Rooney to the stage. Shows run from Feb. 4-8 in the Highmark Theatre and tickets can be purchased online.

Enter the promo code CHIEF1933 before selecting your show date and time. “It’s wonderfully fitting that our Founder’s Day weekend celebrates two legendary Pittsburgh beginnings — the founding of both Point Park University and the Pittsburgh Steelers in 1933,” Brussalis said. “We’re delighted to bring 'The Chief' back to the stage — a timeless tribute to leadership, grit and the spirit that defines our city.” #### President’s Distinguished Achievement Awards The President’s Distinguished Achievement Awards include three different categories, with two people being honored for each one. The **Green Citation** is awarded to distinguished individuals whose exemplary service to Point Park University reflects remarkable dedication and lasting impact. The inaugural honorees are **Dave Duncan** and **Ed Haberle** , both 1979 graduates of Point Park and members of the 1979 baseball team, which was inducted into the school’s Athletics Hall of Fame. Duncan, executive chairman of Duncan Financial Group, is a longtime member of the school’s Board of Trustees. Haberle, a longtime executive at Nike, also is a current member of the Board. The **Gold Citation** is awarded to individuals whose outstanding professional or volunteer achievements bring distinction and honor to Point Park University. The inaugural honorees are **Anne Lewis** and **Don Kelly**. Lewis, board chair of Oxford Development Co., is a former chair of the school’s Board of Trustees and an emeritus member of the board. Kelly, manager of the Pittsburgh Pirates, is a 2006 graduate of Point Park and was a member of the school’s baseball team. He was inducted into Point Park’s Athletics Hall of Fame in 2009.

The Presidential Medal of Honor is Point Park’s highest tribute — a recognition of those whose vision, integrity, and lifelong devotion to excellence embody the very spirit of the institution. The inaugural honorees are **Jerry McGinnis** and **Tom Golonski**. McGinnis, who passed away in 2024, founded Respironics, a medical device company that sold the first mass-produced CPAP machines. He was chair of the Board of Trustees for Point Park during a turbulent time in the 1970s, and his leadership helped keep the school afloat. Golonski, a 1975 Point Park graduate, was CEO of National City Bank and an Independent Director at Black Box Corp. title: Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre
text:
Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre
# Meet the Team ### Quantum Theatre’s work thrives thanks to the collaboration of a strong administrative team and experienced production crew who specialize in site-specific work to support ambitious programming. ##### Executive Director ### Julie DeSeyn Julie is an accomplished nonprofit executive with more than two decades of leadership experience across the arts, human services, philanthropy, and community development. She brings deep expertise in building sustainable business models, fostering collaborative and high-performing teams, and advancing ambitious goals with limited resources. Known for her creative and innovative approach to problem-solving, Julie excels at cultivating community partnerships, strengthening trust, and leading effective fundraising efforts. She has served as Executive Director of Quantum since February 2023. ##### Associate Director ### Nate Madden Nate graduated from the University of Pittsburgh in 2023 with a BA in Religious Studies. He manages Quantum Theatre’s data and development processes and oversees patron experience operations. ##### Associate Director ### Kelley Bowen Kelley studied theatre at The College of William & Mary and Boston University. She began her professional career as an actress in Pittsburgh, and as an assistant director with the Three Rivers Shakespeare Festival and Boston’s Huntington Theatre Company.

title: Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre
text:
Meet the Team - Quantum Theatre
Kelley studied theatre at The College of William & Mary and Boston University. She began her professional career as an actress in Pittsburgh, and as an assistant director with the Three Rivers Shakespeare Festival and Boston’s Huntington Theatre Company. After film, tv, and commercial work in Los Angeles, she held development and literary roles at South Coast Repertory and Merrimack Repertory Theatre, and now supports communication, events, and community partnerships at Quantum. ##### Associate Producer and Patron Relations Manager ### Hazy J Hazy is a Youngstown State University alumnus with their BFA in Theatre Studies and a minor in Music. Hazy has worked professionally as a house manager and stage manager in Pittsburgh and Youngstown for more than five years and is proud to work with the administrative and production teams to continuously improve the patron experience. ##### Director of Production ### Alex Ungerman Alex Ungerman has directed 48 plays and produced 60. His work has appeared at Fringe Festivals around the country, and twice at the Edinburgh Fringe. He co-founded _The Grassroots Shakespeare Company_ in 2009–which has produced Shakespeare around the world, including: Utah, Arizona, Washington D.C., and London.

His work has appeared at Fringe Festivals around the country, and twice at the Edinburgh Fringe. He co-founded _The Grassroots Shakespeare Company_ in 2009–which has produced Shakespeare around the world, including: Utah, Arizona, Washington D.C., and London. He also led _Sackerson_ , an award-winning Salt Lake City immersive company dedicated to producing new work in unconventional spaces for bold audiences. Before coming to Quantum, he served as Associate Artistic Director at Birmingham Children’s Theatre–the second oldest continually operating professional theatre for young audiences in the U.S. Nothing thrills him more than bringing live audiences into magical spaces for unforgettable stories. ##### Technical Specialist ### Anthony Del Grosso Anthony facilitates the technical needs of the sound, lighting, and video departments and acts as production sound mixer for Quantum’s productions. A Maryland native, Anthony moved to Pittsburgh in 2017 to attend Duquesne University, graduating in 2021 with a Bachelor of Music in Music Technology. In addition to his work as a technician, Anthony also occasionally freelances as a sound designer and composer. ##### Technical Director ### James “Cubbie” McCrory Cubbie is thrilled to cultivate and collaborate on unique and adventurous theatre here in his hometown of Pittsburgh.

title: The Museum - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:
The Museum - The Andy Warhol Museum
We are one of the most comprehensive single-artist museums in the world and the largest in North America. The Warhol is one of the four Carnegie Museums, and a collaborative project between Carnegie Institute, Dia Art Foundation, and The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Inc. Plans to house The Warhol in Pittsburgh were announced in 1989, and the museum opened its doors during a 24-hour celebration on May 13, 1994. Originally built in 1911 as a distribution center for products sold to mills and mines, The Warhol was redesigned by architect Richard Gluckman and features seven floors of gallery and exhibition space as well as an underground level that houses The Factory education studio and the conservation lab. Established in 1895 by Andrew Carnegie, Carnegie Museums is a collection of four distinct museums: Carnegie Museum of Art, Carnegie Museum of Natural History, Kamin Science Center, and The Andy Warhol Museum. The museums reach more than 1.4 million people a year through exhibitions, educational programs, outreach activities, and special events.

The museum also houses the entire Andy Warhol Video Collection – over 2,300 videotapes which include all episodes and outtakes of his television series _Fashion_ , _Andy Warhol’s T.V._ , and _Andy Warhol’s_ _Fifteen Minutes_ , the soap operas _Vivian’s Girls_ , _Phoney_ , and _Fight_ , and the large body of work known as _Factory Diaries_. The film and video collection is critical to understanding the artist Andy Warhol. From the time he obtained his first film camera in 1963 until his death in 1987, Warhol actively explored the moving image, creating epic films, personal portraits, cable television shows, and music videos. His films and video capture the rich and raw texture of the fertile cultural milieu in which he lived and worked. title: The Collection - The Andy Warhol Museum
text:
The Collection - The Andy Warhol Museum
## The museum The museum’s collection includes works from the artist’s entire artistic output—from 1940s student work to 1980s collaborations. Our seven-story museum devotes four floors to showcasing an ever-changing selection of Warhol’s artwork, as well as features a permanent film and video gallery for viewing individual Warhol films and videos. One floor is devoted to the museum’s archives collection, and another is reserved for rotating exhibitions of deep dives into the museum’s collection or showcasing contemporary artists that resonate with Warhol. The ground floor continuously shows Fifteen Minutes Eternal, a twenty-minute introductory film, and the underground includes The Factory education studio and the museum’s conservation lab. ## Exhibition Rentals Our curatorial team develops traveling exhibitions that are available to rent for display at museums around the world. #### **Parking and Shuttles –****Schenley Park** Public parking is available on Flagstaff Hill, across the street from Phipps Conservatory, on the July 18/19, 2026 weekend. Free air-conditioned shuttle buses will take you to the golf course and over to the Paddock and the Start/Finish line. #### **Cost** * Cars: $20 per day – does not include a weekend wristband * Vehicles over 25′ long: $50 per day – includes 1 weekend wristband Your donation will benefit our charities. The parking lot opens at 8:00 AM, and shuttles run from 8:00 AM until 6:00 PM. Credit cards are accepted on-site. You can purchase your parking pass in advance**Here** **GoogleMap link to Flagstaff Hill** #### Handicap Parking & Accessibility We have a designated area at the base of Flagstaff Hill by the shuttle stop near Carnegie Mellon University for handicap parking. Public parking is $20 for each day, but does not include your weekend Gate Pass, which is $20. We also have a handicap shuttle bus to transport you up to the golf course. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix is committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming experience for all guests.

Please note that our event is held on a golf course that does not have paved cart paths or permanent accessible routes. As a result, access across the grounds may be limited for guests with mobility impairments, especially in inclement weather. Designated handicap parking spaces will be available as close as possible to the main event areas, subject to space and ground conditions. A valid state-issued disability parking placard or license plate is required to use these spaces. Please be aware that golf carts and personal transportation vehicles are **not** available for rent or use on-site. Guests are encouraged to plan accordingly and bring any necessary personal mobility aids, such as wheelchairs or walkers, that are suitable for grass and uneven terrain. This shuttle departs Flagstaff Hill, goes up Frew Street and stops along Schenley Drive before returning via Forbes Avenue. text:
Blacktie & Tailpipes Gala Pittsburgh | PVGP
# Black Tie & Tailpipes Gala Saturday, July 11, 2026 Our Black Tie & Tailpipes Gala opens Grand Prix Race Week in formal style! This is a must for any auto enthusiast who enjoys shiny cars, fine dining and great company. In addition to being one of the city’s best summer parties, it is also a significant fundraiser for our charity partners. History will be made in 2026 as the Gala moves to the Kamin Science Center, where Chair Ev Kelly Searle is already planning an unforgettable evening. The event shifts into high gear with exclusive behind-the-scenes access to _Science of Speed_ , an incredible experience showcasing the physics, innovation, and technology behind the world’s fastest machines. Guests will also get a special preview of the exciting two-story electric kart track, scheduled to officially open to the public on August 1. Live entertainment provided by The Commonheart. They bring an electrifying blend of soul, rock, and blues that has made them one of Pittsburgh’s most dynamic live acts. Known for their high-energy performances and powerful vocals, the band delivers a rich, authentic sound that gets crowds on their feet and keeps them there.

text:

3:30 Preservation & Pre-War ## Midday Action: Three Exciting Exhibition Groups This year, the lunch break becomes part of the action as the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix introduces three exciting Exhibition Groups. Located in front of Phipps Conservatory, the exhibition paddock offers spectators a rare opportunity to meet the participants, get up close to the vehicles, and experience the excitement before they take to the course. These unique attractions bring added energy and entertainment to race weekend and are not to be missed. #### BMW Ring Taxi Buckle up and experience the PVGP from the passenger seat of the BMW Ring Taxi. It’s the fastest, loudest, and most exhilarating ride of race weekend. Inspired by the famous passenger rides at Germany’s Nürburgring, the Ring Taxi gives fans the opportunity to ride the famous Schenley Park circuit in a high-performance BMW M car. From the acceleration up the hills to the dramatic turns and elevation changes, passengers experience the course exactly as the racers do. The Ring Taxi has become one of the PVGP’s most popular attractions, drawing crowds to the snow fence to watch the BMW slide through Schenley Park’s corners – delivering passengers an unforgettable ride.

title: PVGP Race Rules & Safety Regulations | Schenley Park
text:
PVGP Race Rules & Safety Regulations | Schenley Park
# Racers Rules & Regulations **It is each competitor’s responsibility to understand and comply with all Rules and Regulations which apply to their car. Non-compliance may result in exclusion or disqualification. Ignorance of these rules is not a valid defense.** Vintage sports car racing is an amateur sport in which competition is intended to be friendly and casual. However, all forms of motorsports are dangerous; therefore, we have developed the following operating procedures to help you understand what action should be taken under certain circumstances. Your knowledge and application of this information are vital to a safe event. ##### 1. Standard Operating Procedures A. **Official Race Control** is through the PVGP Chief Steward and the marshals or other recognized workers. You must comply with their instructions. The PVGP will rule on all infractions of racecourse conduct. B. **Race Procedure** Grids for the races will be determined by your qualifying times and qualifying race results. PVGP reserves the right to slot cars into the grid in the interest of safety. Chief Steward’s decisions are final. In the event of inclement weather during qualifying, grids will be established by PVGPA Officials.

title: PVGP Race Rules & Safety Regulations | Schenley Park
text:
PVGP Race Rules & Safety Regulations | Schenley Park
Chief Steward’s decisions are final. In the event of inclement weather during qualifying, grids will be established by PVGPA Officials. Race lengths shown on the schedule are subject to change due to scheduling constraints, weather conditions and unforeseen circumstances. Changes are announced at the Driver’s Meeting, on the PA system or on the grid. C. **Tech Inspection** Tech inspection hours and location will be stated on the official schedule. Your Tech sheets are located at Tech and Race Registration. Have your correctly assigned race number on your car and an AMB transponder installed adequately before you arrive at Tech.**PVGP Tech Sheet 2026** D. **False Grid** Cars arriving after the five-minute signal may forfeit grid position. You may be required to join your session from pit out if you arrive after the grid closes. Do not attempt to regain your original grid position during the pace lap. No one under the age of 16 is permitted on the grid. Open-toed shoes are not allowed. E. **Pit Entry and Exit** should be at moderate or slow speed. Pit speeds will be announced at the driver’s meeting. The maximum speed allowed will be 10 mph.

Extra caution is required whenever you are passing or being passed. Responsibility for a clean pass rests with both drivers, with the primary responsibility on the overtaking car. Corner stations will advise slower cars with a blue flag (passing flag. Watch your mirrors. If practicable, the overtaken driver should clearly indicate to the overtaking driver on which side the pass should be made while maintaining a predictable racing line. There is absolutely no passing under a yellow flag. G. **Safety Car** If the safety car enters the circuit, slow down and follow in a single file. Do not change position and do not pass the safety car unless waved by. H. **Black Flag & Meatball **(Black Flag with Orange Ball – mechanical problem) will be displayed at Flag Station 18 (top of Serpentine) and may also be displayed at Start/Finish. If you are Black Flagged or shown the Meatball, pull into the Pits and wait for an official to clear you to resume driving.

title: History Of The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Through Our Posters
text:
History Of The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Through Our Posters
# History of the PVGP **The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix is well known for the posters we create each year…so we thought that the best way to tell the story of our event is through the posters.** Each poster captures the beauty and excitement of our event. We have been fortunate enough to have the artwork donated each year by both local and national artists. The first event was the brainchild of Art McGovern and Mary Beth Gmitter who, in 1982, carpooled together. Art dreamed of holding a race through the streets of Schenley Park. The first meetings were held in Alan Patterson’s garage in Shadyside. A group quickly formed, comprised of racers, Sports Car Club of America members and other interested parties including Myron Cope of WTAE. In 1982 the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Association was founded and designated a nonprofit organization incorporated for the express purpose of sponsoring the race. They, along with many other volunteers to follow, set out to run the first vintage race in Schenley Park, made available for the event by Pittsburgh Mayor Richard Caliguiri. and CitiParks’ Louise Brown and Carl Mancuso.

title: History Of The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Through Our Posters
text:
History Of The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Through Our Posters
In 1982 the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Association was founded and designated a nonprofit organization incorporated for the express purpose of sponsoring the race. They, along with many other volunteers to follow, set out to run the first vintage race in Schenley Park, made available for the event by Pittsburgh Mayor Richard Caliguiri. and CitiParks’ Louise Brown and Carl Mancuso. The first race was launched in September of 1983 and the story continues today as we prepare for the 44th Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix in 2026. **To Order Posters Click Here** ## **1983** On Labor Day, 1983, 80 entrants – including 14 from Canada – came to race on what would become a hallmark vintage racing track that wound through Pittsburgh’s Schenley Park. Alan Patterson served as our first Race Director and helped recruit the racers. A small group of dedicated volunteers and Steel Cities SCCA members worked furiously to stage the event and create the race circuit. Five races were scheduled along with a parade of patrons to start the day of racing. All events were held on one hectic September Saturday. After the closure of the Panther Hollow Bridge forced the PVGP to create alternate racing formats in 2025, the bridge reopened for Race Weekend and vintage racers once again competed over the complete 2.33-mile, 22-turn course through the park. Jaguar returned as Marque of the Year for the fifth time, and the celebration became truly international as the Jaguar Clubs of North America brought the International Jaguar Festival to Pittsburgh. Nearly 200 Jaguars participated throughout the weekend, with acclaimed automotive designer Ian Callum crossing the Atlantic to serve as Grand Marshal.

title: History Of The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Through Our Posters
text:
History Of The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Through Our Posters
Jaguar returned as Marque of the Year for the fifth time, and the celebration became truly international as the Jaguar Clubs of North America brought the International Jaguar Festival to Pittsburgh. Nearly 200 Jaguars participated throughout the weekend, with acclaimed automotive designer Ian Callum crossing the Atlantic to serve as Grand Marshal. Callum was a fixture throughout Race Week, meeting racers and enthusiasts, participating in events and waving the checkered flag at Schenley Park. The International Car Show once again filled the Bob O’Connor Golf Course with thousands of classic, exotic and enthusiast vehicles. Pontiac and Oakland celebrated their 100th anniversary as the 2026 Spotlight, while British Car Day, the Italian Cortile and the growing Enthusiast Grid helped create one of the most diverse automotive gatherings in the event’s history. There was new energy on the racecourse as well. Drifting demonstrations brought a completely different style of motorsport to Schenley Park, Formula SAE teams showcased the engineering talent of university students, and BMW Performance Center instructor Mike Renner thrilled spectators with charity rides around the circuit in the BMW Ring Taxi. Despite traffic challenges from the Parkway East closure, spectators turned out in impressive numbers.

# Asian Car Show ##### **Weekend July 17-18, 2027** The Asian Car Show continues to grow each year and has quickly become one of the most exciting and diverse displays at Schenley Park. From iconic Japanese classics to modern performance cars, this show celebrates the full spectrum of Asian automotive culture. Today, the field features a strong and enthusiastic mix of Subaru, Mazda, Nissan and Datsun, Honda, Acura, Mitsubishi and Suzuki, with everything from beautifully preserved originals to modified and track-inspired builds. It is a dynamic display that reflects both heritage and innovation. We warmly welcome all Asian marques and enthusiast groups to be part of this expanding community. Whether you are an individual owner or represent a car club, there is a place for you here. If your group would like to establish its own featured display, please reach out to Tim Gilkey. We would love to work with you to grow this show even further and showcase your cars alongside some of the best in the region. ##### Location

# Tune-Up @ SouthSide Works Wednesday, July 14, 2027 The PVGP looks forward to celebrating our 45th year in 2027 by partying SouthSide Style for our annual Tune-Up as we prepare for the races and car show just a few days later. Hundreds of cars will gather for a fabulous car show, featuring race cars, exotics, antiques, and show cars, at this exciting street festival in the streets surrounding the SouthSide Works Town Square. We are looking forward to another great evening on the South Side! ## Registration Opens in 2027 **_Registration closes on Monday, July 12, at noon. Entries will not be accepted after that, and you cannot pay at the event._** Participation in this year’s Tune-Up Party is still just $50. You get a reserved parking spot within the Automotive Showcase on the streets of the SouthSide Works. Two drink coupons for the driver, redeemable at any drink station, are included. You can also register any guests for $25 each, and they will also receive two complimentary drink coupons. There are plenty of great places to Eat & Drink in Town Square. The PVGP will also have drink trucks available.

# Porsche Club Car Show ##### **Weekend July 17-18, 2027** Plan to attend the 44th annual Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix with the Allegheny Region Porsche Club of America. Join hundreds of your fellow club members, guests from other regions, and friends as they gather on “**Porsche Field** ” in Schenley Park to enjoy fine automotive culture, vintage races, and the camaraderie that defines PVGP weekend. This year promises to be an outstanding event featuring a multitude of Porsche Club and PVGP events spanning nine days. **Porsche Field** patrons enjoy high-quality amenities, including a catered lunch from Mission BBQ, Dining and Registration tents replete with linen tablecloths, cooling fans, and unlimited non-alcoholic beverages, live music, high-value raffle prizes, and People’s Choice Awards. The club’s PVGP Committee uses a streamlined check-in process in which attendees register through Motorsport Registration (MSR) and receive an email from __**PVGP_Reg@arpca.com**__ with a dash plaque and a QR code “ticket” as attachments. As members drive up to the Porsche Field, volunteers scan the QR code and have wrist bands, raffle tickets, and the PVGP program pre-staged at the Registration tent. ## Porsche Club Leads PVGP 2020 Fundraising Efforts

# "Evening of Speed" Drivers Reception Friday, July 17, 2026 Kick off Race Weekend the right way, right at trackside. The Drivers Reception returned to the Schenley Park Visitor’s Center for the first time since 2021, and there’s no better place to start your weekend. Located beside the Panther Hollow Bridge and directly along the course, this is your chance to step out of the paddock and into the spotlight, surrounded by fellow racers, crews, and fans who appreciate what you bring to the streets of Schenley Park. From 6:30 PM to 8:00 PM, the track in front of the Visitor’s Center becomes a gathering point for the entire racing community. Cars on display, stories shared, and a relaxed atmosphere that lets you connect with other drivers before the competition begins. At 6:30 PM, racers will parade from the paddock around the circuit to the reception. They will park their race cars trackside in front of the Visitor’s Center for all to see, with the option to arrive in a support vehicle instead. Thanks to Broad Arrow Auctions, A Hagerty Company, this is a complimentary event for participants.

title: About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
text:
About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
**_The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix is the nation’s only vintage street race and the largest vintage race event. It includes car shows, parties, parades and motorsport events with the culmination each July in Schenley Park._** Our original mission, established in 1983, was “To stage a world-class vintage automotive event to raise funds to provide care, treatment and support for individuals with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities in western Pennsylvania.” 44 years later, we are still on track. Though our first race was in 1983, our organization actually started the year prior. Art McGovern and Mary Beth Gmitter envisioned the city streets winding through Schenley Park as a perfect venue for vintage auto racing. Told that the City of Pittsburgh’s approval hinged on the assurance that any money raised would go to charity, they first approached Myron Cope of WTAE-TV Sports fame – also an autism awareness advocate. Meetings with the city’s parks people followed, and then-Mayor Richard Caliguiri gave his enthusiastic approval. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Association, consisting of volunteers, was created, and net proceeds would be donated to charity.

title: About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
text:
About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
Meetings with the city’s parks people followed, and then-Mayor Richard Caliguiri gave his enthusiastic approval. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Association, consisting of volunteers, was created, and net proceeds would be donated to charity. In April 1983, during a meeting in vintage racer Alan Patterson’s Shadyside garage, the planning began for the first Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, scheduled for Labor Day 1983. An incredible amount of work ensued thanks to the volunteers from the Sports Car Club of America and the Vintage Sports Car Club of America. Some 75 entrants raced on what would become known as one of the most challenging vintage courses in the country. Five races, along with a parade of patrons, were scheduled, and the plan was put in motion. We would be lying if we said that the first year went off without a hitch. The complications of a temporary track in the middle of one of Pittsburgh’s most popular public parks reared their heads almost immediately. Huge fence gaps and the labyrinth of infield trails left the course open to penetration from above and below. Recreational joggers were running with the cars zooming around the track.

title: About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
text:
About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
Huge fence gaps and the labyrinth of infield trails left the course open to penetration from above and below. Recreational joggers were running with the cars zooming around the track. Our volunteer security struggled to overcome these logistical challenges. Nonetheless, the event was a success. The experience only fueled our imaginations and motivations, and in 1984 the expansion began. We added an invitational car show and the Sunday tailgate known as Patron Parking. By 1985, our spectator count grew to 40,000 and included participants and fans from all over North America as well as Europe. The genesis of Race Week, in 1987, was ushered in with our first Kick-Off Rallye the preceding Sunday. Our volunteer army grew by leaps and bounds and by 1989 we reached 1,000 volunteers – many of whom still volunteer to this day. Race Week spectator draw has consistently grown throughout the years and is now estimated at close to a quarter-million. With the added size came added attention – from Pittsburgh and beyond. In 1996, Buick signed on as our first Presenting Sponsor. They also brought new models and concept cars to the event and helped legitimize our stature within the auto industry.

title: About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity

About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
In 1996, Buick signed on as our first Presenting Sponsor. They also brought new models and concept cars to the event and helped legitimize our stature within the auto industry. Modern race cars from the Indy 500, Le Mans, and elsewhere have blasted down the Boulevard of the Allies and snaked between Serpentine’s stone walls. Ferrari, Marque of the Year in 1993, showed up with museum-piece cars and actually put them on the track – in the rain. In 1994, Marque of the Year one-upmanship began as each attempted to better the proceeding’s donations and spectacle. The gauntlet, first thrown down by Porsche, has been eagerly picked up by BMW, Mustang, MINI and others since then. In 2018 BMW set the Marque record with $126,500 raised only to be surpassed the next year by Ford Mustang & Shelby with $132,500! Shop ‘n Save took over the Presenting Sponsorship from 2001 through 2013, which oversaw many events being added to occupy 10 straight days of motorsport events. Sponsorship began to grow significantly after that and has led to a larger show, resulting in increased charity donations.

Shop ‘n Save took over the Presenting Sponsorship from 2001 through 2013, which oversaw many events being added to occupy 10 straight days of motorsport events. Sponsorship began to grow significantly after that and has led to a larger show, resulting in increased charity donations. In 2004, the second weekend of racing was added at Pittsburgh International Race Complex, and it has developed into a self-supportive historic racing event for newer historic bug-bore cars that are too fast for the city streets of Schenley Park. Pitt Race closed down after the 2025 season, marking the end of 22 great years of racing. A black-tie gala was launched in 1997 and has since become a staple of the Pittsburgh summer social scene, ranking among our largest fundraisers. Our Tune-Up party was created in 2006 and has grown into a tremendous event that has since moved to the SouthSide Works. The Greater Pittsburgh Automobile Dealers Foundation took the wheel as our presenting sponsor in 2014 and the partnership has driven our greatest growth and success through 2022. A Countryside Tour was started and filled Thursday, the last remaining Race Week open day.

About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
The Greater Pittsburgh Automobile Dealers Foundation took the wheel as our presenting sponsor in 2014 and the partnership has driven our greatest growth and success through 2022. A Countryside Tour was started and filled Thursday, the last remaining Race Week open day. In 2017 a Jet Center Party was added, elevating our event to the top tier of worldwide automotive events. In 2018 we hosted the BMW Oktoberfest and in 2019 the national car clubs for Shelby and Alfa Romeo held their conventions at the PVGP. We are pleased that they chose to celebrate with us. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix has continued to grow while adapting to major challenges and welcoming significant automotive milestones. A highlight was the Shelby Convention’s visit in 2018, which included the unveiling of the 760-horsepower 2020 Ford GT500 during the downtown car show and displays throughout Race Week. In 2020, the pandemic forced the cancellation of Race Week events, but the PVGP responded with the “Shifting Gears” initiative, encouraging car clubs to hold smaller driving events. More than two dozen gatherings raised $60,000 for charity.

title: About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity

About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
In 2020, the pandemic forced the cancellation of Race Week events, but the PVGP responded with the “Shifting Gears” initiative, encouraging car clubs to hold smaller driving events. More than two dozen gatherings raised $60,000 for charity. In 2021, Vintage Indy returned with historic Indy 500 cars and two-time winner Al Unser Jr. as Honorary Race Director. Subsequent years featured notable guests and specialty races, including Porsche executive Ray Shaffer as Grand Marshal, a Viper spotlight with Team Viper, and the Kastner Cup Triumph race. In 2023, Shelby Daytona designer Peter Brock and Grand Marshal Luigi Chinetti Jr. praised the event’s authentic vintage racing atmosphere. Recent highlights include the GT40 Reunion, Ragtime Racers exhibitions, and the debut of the Grand Prix Garden Party at Phipps Conservatory. In 2025 we hosted the Panoz Reunion at Pittsburgh International Race Complex – on of the last events at the track before it was closed. When the Panther Hollow Bridge closed in 2025, the PVGP created new race layouts, demonstrating the organization’s creativity and resilience while continuing to earn international recognition. Accolades continue to grow. Classic Motorsports Magazine honored the PVGP as a winner in its inaugural Editors’ Choice Awards.

About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
Accolades continue to grow. Classic Motorsports Magazine honored the PVGP as a winner in its inaugural Editors’ Choice Awards. This distinction adds to the event’s expanding international recognition, including its third consecutive nomination as a finalist for “Motorsport Event of the Year” by the International Historic Motoring Awards. All the while, we’ve held true to our charity mission –to produce a world-class vintage automotive event to raise funds to help provide residential care, treatment and support for autistic and intellectually/developmentally disabled individuals in the Pittsburgh region. It has been over 40 years since a cadre of car nuts met in Alan Patterson’s Shadyside garage, and each year brings its challenges. Our volunteers remain the heart of the organization and the event, with over 1,000 dedicated individuals working year-round to stage this incredible event. Much credit also goes to our sponsors, racers and participants who share their cars to make our event possible. title: Pontiac/Oakland - 2026 Spotlight Car | PVGP
text:
Pontiac/Oakland - 2026 Spotlight Car | PVGP
# ******Pontiac & Oakland – 100th Anniversary Spotlight Car Show 2026 Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix** A century ago, Pontiac changed the game. In 2026, it takes over Schenley Park. For Pontiac owners and enthusiasts who have never experienced the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, this is your moment. While PVGP is known worldwide for its vintage racing, at its heart, it is a celebration of all car culture—and this year, American performance takes center stage. The Pontiac & Oakland 100th Anniversary Spotlight invites you to be part of something bigger than a traditional car show: a full-scale festival where your car is not just displayed, it is part of the story. Bring your GTO, LeMans, Bonneville, Firebird, Trans Am, Grand Prix, Fiero, Safari wagons, or your Oakland-era classic and park it on the fairways alongside thousands of fellow enthusiasts. You’ll be surrounded by 3,000 show cars, 100,000+ spectators, and the unmistakable energy of race weekend—vintage race cars charging through the park just steps away, crowds lining the course, and a setting unlike anything else in the country. This is not a foreign sports car show. This is a celebration of performance, heritage, and passion—where Pontiac’s legacy belongs front and center.

# BMW Car Show and Club Gathering **The PVGP and BMW CCA Allegheny Chapter are excited to host BMW as the 2027 Marque of the Year! Adding to the excitement, the BMW CCA will be bringing its O’Fest gathering to Pittsburgh. And to top it off, the BMW Classic Car Club of America will be making the PVGP its focus event for 2027. This promises to be an incredible week for all car enthusiasts! A full schedule of MOY and O’Fest events will be announced in the coming months, but save the date on your calendar: July 10-18, 2027! YOU’VE GOT TO BE HERE!** The BMW Car Club of America’s Allegheny Chapter has long been one of the most passionate and impactful participants in the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, bringing an unmistakable energy and presence to German Hill each July. Known for their warm hospitality and innovative programming, the club has also set the benchmark for Marque of the Year fundraising – highlighted by a record-setting $126,500 contribution in 2018 and more than $425,000 raised in support of PVGP charities.

title: Pittsburgh BMW Car Show | PVGP BMW Club Gathering
text:
Pittsburgh BMW Car Show | PVGP BMW Club Gathering
Honorary Race Director and BMW racer Bill Auberlen takes his BMW Z4 GTLM around the track on an exhibition lap at Schenley Park in 2018. **Special Volunteers: Mike Renner and his BMW Ring Taxi** Ever wondered what it’s like to experience the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix from inside the snow fence beside the action? Each year, Mike Renner delivers that thrill with the BMW Ring Taxi – one of the most popular attractions at Schenley Park. Inspired by the legendary Sabine Schmitz and her high-speed passenger laps at the Nürburgring, the BMW CCA Allegheny Chapter brought the Ring Taxi concept to the PVGP in 2009. Mike, an instructor from the BMW Performance Center, volunteered – and the response was immediate. Since then, Mike has returned every year, giving charity laps in the latest BMW performance cars and occasionally pre-production models. His runs, often during lunch and between race groups, have become a must-see (and must-ride) experience. Just as important, Mike continues to support the PVGP’s mission by donating BMW Performance Center driving schools and auction items, helping raise thousands of dollars annually for our charity partners.

A skilled racer and instructor, Mike makes it look dramatic – especially sliding through Turn 13 – but he’s always in control. More than that, he’s embraced the spirit of the PVGP, sharing his passion with fans and representing the event wherever he goes. If you get the chance to ride along, take it. It’s one of the most unforgettable experiences of the weekend. Mike takes the Ring Taxi into a turn at Schenley Park The PVGP is one of Mike’s favorite events. He said: “I love coming to the PVGP because of the unique nature of the event. The city does such a great job making the event happen. Everyone involved is incredibly friendly and welcoming. # Trailer Parking ## Trailer Parking for Car Show Participants – July 17/18, 2027 The growth of our International Car Show at Schenley Park has helped elevate our event to new heights, but with 3,000 show cars, there is no space on the golf course to park trailers and tow vehicles. Schenley Park is in a tightly congested area with limited parking options, so if you decide to bring your car on a trailer, you have limited options during the event: **Option 1: Flagstaff Hill Parking ** You must pay $50 daily to park your trailer and tow vehicle on Flagstaff Hill. This is the large, gently sloping grass hill across the street from Phipps Conservatory—see image below. You must enter from Schenley Drive after crossing the bridge from Schenley Plaza. We suggest using Phipps Conservatory as the GPS location. Once you have paid and parked, you can unload your car and drive it up to the golf course. Details on Flagstaff Hill Parking. **Option 2: Surface Parking Lots ** Limited parking lots in Oakland accommodate a trailer with a tow vehicle. **Flagstaff Hill Parking is shown in the middle of the image. Phipps Conservatory is at the bottom.**

# Countryside Tour Thursday, July 16, 2026 Flickr Gallery for Countryside Tour – Click the image above to view the entire album If driving your classic sports car is your main passion, we invite you to join us for the Countryside Tour. Participation is limited to sports & GT cars produced in 1983 and earlier* Bud Osbourne conceived the Countryside Tour in 2012 as part of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. Bud has handed over the reins to Derek Kuntz and Marla Taylor-Kuntz. The tour follows a delightful collection of scenic, twisting, lightly traveled back roads through Pennsylvania’s beautiful Laurel Highlands. Be advised that this is a DRIVING tour and not for the faint of heart. We cover many miles, and it’s all back roads at a brisk pace! **Schedule – Thursday, July 16, 2026** First Group Starts: 9:00 AM from Liberty Pole Spirits Lunch at Jamison Farm: 1:00 – 2:30 PM The 2026 Countryside Tour will kick off from Liberty Pole Spirits in Washington, PA (800 Adios Drive Washington, PA 15301). Registration will begin at 8:00am.

# Mercedes-Benz Car Show ##### Weekend, July 17/18, 2027 Mark Sheldon, a longtime and active member of the Mercedes-Benz Club and a familiar face at the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, was seriously injured while volunteering during this year’s PVGP. Mark has given generously of his time and energy to our automotive community, and now he and his family could use our support. Please consider making a donation to help with the expenses associated with his recovery and rehabilitation. For generations, the Mercedes-Benz Club of America Pittsburgh Section has been a passionate supporter of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and its charitable mission. Mercedes-Benz enthusiasts are invited to join us for an impressive display celebrating the elegance, engineering, and performance that define the marque. From timeless classics to modern luxury and AMG performance models, this gathering showcases the rich heritage and enduring appeal of Mercedes-Benz. Whether you are a longtime club member, a first-time participant, or simply a fan of the brand, you are welcome to be part of the experience. While membership in the Mercedes-Benz Club is encouraged, it is not required to participate.

Pittsburgh Garden Party At Phipps Conservatory | PVGP
# Grand Prix Garden Party at Phipps Conservatory Thursday, July 16, 2026 This year’s event will feature a curated display of concours-quality automobiles on the front lawn of the Phipps Conservatory. Guests can expect a stunning selection of vehicles. With Jaguar as the Marque of the Year for the and the International Jaguar Festival taking place during PVGP Race Week, along with our Pontiac Spotlight, we are seeking historically significant Jaguars to display at the Garden Party. If you own a historically significant Jaguar, please send a photo and a brief description to Bob Speer for consideration by our committee for the special display in front of Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens. A second dedicated parking area will also be available for the other Jaguars which can be displayed together during the event. PVGP Marque Of The Year History | Pittsburgh Car Show
# Marque & Spotlight History The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix began the practice of honoring a specific car brand beginning with our third race back in 1985. Many of auto racing’s preeminent manufacturers have been recognized at our event. French for “brand,” marque (pronounced “mark”) refers to a brand name given to a line of automobiles. For example, Mercedes-Benz is a marque, whereas the Mercedes-Benz 560SL is a make of the Mercedes-Benz marque. Industry consolidation has slightly clouded this designation, but marque is still used to define a particular line of vehicles. It is a term typically reserved, however, for the more prestigious motoring brands. ### PVGP Marques of the Year 1985 Lotus 1986 Jaguar 1987 Morgan 1988 Lancia 1989 Mercedes-Benz 1990 Alfa Romeo 1991 MG 1992 Ferrari 1993 Corvette 1994 Porsche 1995 Austin-Healey 1996 Jaguar 1997 15th Anniversary – all Marques 1998 BMW 1999 Mercedes-Benz 2000 Audi/Auto Union 2001 Bentley 2002 Porsche 2003 Corvette 2004 Mini Cooper 2005 Mustang 2006 Jaguar 2007 Mercedes-Benz 2008 Italian Cars 2009 BMW 2010 Audi 2011 Porsche 2012 MG 2013 Ford Mustang 2014 Mini Cooper 2015 The Cars of Italy 2016 Jaguar 2017 Camaro 2018 BMW 2019 Shelby & Mustang 2021 Corvette 2022 Porsche
